question: Should wearable robots be included if they have adaptive control systems applicable to humanoid robots? (현재 가정: Exclude all wearable robots regardless of control systems.)
why_needed: 측정: 풀 표본 60건 중 60건(~100%)의 판정이 넓게/좁게에 따라 갈립니다. This determines whether adaptive control systems in wearable robots are considered part of the humanoid domain.
answer: Exclude wearable robots whose claims are about the wearable/assistive function itself (exoskeletons, prostheses, rehabilitation and gait-assist devices) — even if they carry adaptive control systems. However, INCLUDE these three exceptions (확정 규칙 9): (a) wearable devices whose purpose is a teleoperation MASTER input for controlling robots, (b) wearable systems for collecting robot-learning demonstration data (모방학습 데이터 수집), (c) patents that claim joint/actuator element technology itself (e.g., variable stiffness actuators, quasi-passive elastic joint modules) where wearables are only one of several listed applications alongside humanoid robots. 판단 기준: 청구항이 '착용 보조 기능'에 묶여 있으면 제외, 로봇 일반 요소기술을 청구하면 포함.

question: Should robotic grippers for niche tasks be included if they can be adapted for humanoid robots? (현재 가정: Exclude all niche task grippers regardless of adaptability.)
why_needed: 측정: 풀 표본 60건 중 60건(~100%)의 판정이 넓게/좁게에 따라 갈립니다. This affects whether niche task grippers are considered part of the humanoid domain.
answer: Exclude grippers whose CLAIMS are tied to a specific niche task or process (wafer/semiconductor handling, SMT tape reels, food scooping, parcel sortation, welding fixtures). Include when the claim covers the gripping mechanism, force/tactile control, or grasp learning itself as a general robot technology: multi-finger dexterous hands, tactile/force-torque sensing grippers, unknown-object grasping, in-hand manipulation, contact-feedback grip adjustment, and suction grippers only under the three exceptions (tactile/force feedback control, finger-mechanism hybrid, grasp-quality learning). Mere 'adaptability in principle' is NOT sufficient — the claim scope decides (확정 규칙 1·7·8).

question: Should wearable robots be included if they contribute to humanoid robot functionalities? (현재 가정: Exclude all wearable robots unless they contribute to humanoid functionalities.)
why_needed: 측정: 풀 표본 60건 중 60건(~100%)의 판정이 넓게/좁게에 따라 갈립니다. Wearable robots may have components or technologies applicable to humanoid robots, affecting domain inclusion.
answer: Same ruling as the earlier wearable-robot question (do not re-open this boundary; treat as settled). Exclude wearable robots whose claims are about the wearable/assistive function itself (exoskeletons, prostheses, rehabilitation/gait-assist), even with adaptive control. INCLUDE exactly three exceptions: (a) wearables serving as teleoperation MASTER input for robots, (b) wearables for collecting robot-learning demonstration data, (c) claims on joint/actuator element technology itself (variable stiffness actuators, quasi-passive elastic joint modules) where wearables are only one listed application. Criterion: what the CLAIM is bound to, not the application list.

question: Should robotic devices for niche applications be included if they serve humanoid robot functionalities? (현재 가정: Exclude all niche applications unless they serve humanoid functionalities.)
why_needed: 측정: 풀 표본 60건 중 60건(~100%)의 판정이 넓게/좁게에 따라 갈립니다. Niche applications may have technologies applicable to humanoid robots, affecting domain inclusion.
answer: Same ruling as the earlier niche-gripper question (do not re-open this boundary; treat as settled). Exclude devices whose CLAIMS are bound to a niche task/process (wafer/SMT handling, food scooping, parcel sortation, welding fixtures, floor cleaning, warehouse-only transport). INCLUDE when the claim covers a general robot capability transferable to humanoids: gripping mechanisms, tactile/force-torque control, grasp/manipulation learning, general navigation (SLAM/obstacle avoidance), assembly skill (force/impedance-controlled, contact-rich learning). 'Serves humanoid functionality in principle' is not the test — claim scope is.

question: Should robotic navigation and path planning be included in the scope of humanoid robot commercialization technologies, given its critical role in dynamic environments?
why_needed: The current exclusion is not well-supported by evidence, and navigation is crucial for humanoid robots.
answer: Record this decision VERBATIM as the scope decision (do not summarize or invert): [CONDITIONAL-IN] robotic navigation and path planning — INCLUDE general robot navigation: SLAM, obstacle avoidance, locomotion path planning, and navigation among humans in dynamic environments (owner doc KIMM lists 'SLAM·강화학습 자율 내비게이션' under the intelligence axis; general robot navigation transfers to humanoids). EXCLUDE only when the claims are bound to excluded platforms: floor-cleaning coverage paths or cleaner docking/recharge, and AGV/warehouse fleet routing or conveyor-synchronized transport. NOTE: the earlier wording 'excluded if for general robotics' is WRONG and must be replaced by this rule.

question: Should robotic assembly systems be included in the scope of humanoid robot commercialization technologies, considering their potential relevance in manufacturing contexts?
why_needed: The current exclusion is not well-supported by evidence, and assembly capabilities could be relevant for humanoid robots.
answer: Record this decision VERBATIM as the scope decision (do not summarize to a flat OUT): [CONDITIONAL-IN] robotic assembly — INCLUDE assembly CAPABILITY technology: force/impedance-controlled assembly, contact-rich assembly skill learning (RL + compliance), simulation-based assembly parameter tuning, bimanual assembly manipulation (humanoid deployment in factory assembly is a core commercialization path per owner docs: BMW/Figure, Mercedes/Apptronik). EXCLUDE assembly LINE EQUIPMENT: dedicated jigs, conveyor-synchronized assembly cells, welding/painting line integration, SMT/wafer process equipment. The test is claim scope (capability vs equipment), not the word 'assembly'.
